symptom: Agents following the write-workflows skill generated task pages that show the task but have no outcome buttons, so no user could finish the task and every instance stalled at it; the same agents created one microflow per outcome (six for a two-task workflow where Maia made far fewer), explaining that each outcome 'needs a microflow to update the status'. check, mx check and the build were all clean
cause: The skill never mentioned the page action `complete task '<Outcome>'` (Pages$SetTaskOutcomeClientAction), which parses and builds; it said 'there is no `complete task`' (meaning no MICROFLOW statement of that name) and recommended page buttons that call a microflow doing `set task outcome`, i.e. a microflow per outcome
file: `.claude/skills/mendix/write-workflows/SKILL.md` (Task pages section, Microflow statements, Platform rules)
insight: **A sentence scoped to one context is read as global by an agent.** 'There is no complete task' was true of microflows and false of pages, and it steered every generated workflow away from the native button. Before documenting the button as the answer, measure it: on the 11.13.0 runtime (Prototype security, Playwright as the targeted user) a `complete task` button on a task the user is TARGETED for but has not CLAIMED shows 'You can't complete this user task, it is not assigned to you.' and the task stays InProgress — the same rule as `set task outcome` (MDL-WORKFLOW10). With an Assign-to-me microflow (Assignees = [%CurrentUser%]) clicked first, the same button completed the task and the outcome branch ran. So the template carries one shared claim microflow plus one button per outcome, not just the buttons the evaluator asked for. Probe traps: security Off has no user to complete as; a single outcome with a body is CE1876
fix: Skill only: a Task pages section with a measured template (claim microflow, one `complete task` button per outcome, page and microflow grants), the microflow section reworded to say where each form belongs, and a default against mirroring workflow progress into a status attribute with a microflow per transition
